item.title: Escambia, Santa Rosa shellfish areas reopen after water quality review
item.dc:creator: newsroom

The reopening comes after the department completed a water quality review of the affected areas. Shellfish harvesting…
item.content:encoded:
Florida health officials have given the all-clear for shellfish harvesting to resume in portions of Escambia and Santa Rosa Counties, according to an announcement from the Florida Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services.

The reopening comes after the department completed a water quality review of the affected areas. Shellfish harvesting had been restricted in these zones while state officials evaluated conditions to ensure the waters met safety standards for commercial and recreational harvesting.

Local oyster and clam harvesters can now return to these areas. The department's decision reflects improved water quality conditions in the region, though residents should continue to monitor for any future closure notices.

item.title: FPL Completes 2,000 Miles of Underground Power Lines Statewide
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Florida Power & Light has reached a significant infrastructure milestone, completing the conversion of 2,000 miles of overhead power lines to underground across Florida, according to WKRG News 5. The utility's underground conversion program represents an ongoing effort to improve reliability and reduce service disruptions caused by severe weather.…
item.content:encoded:
Florida Power & Light has reached a significant infrastructure milestone, completing the conversion of 2,000 miles of overhead power lines to underground across Florida, according to WKRG News 5.

The utility's underground conversion program represents an ongoing effort to improve reliability and reduce service disruptions caused by severe weather. Underground lines are less vulnerable to damage from high winds, lightning, and falling tree limbs—a major concern in Florida during hurricane season.

Escambia County residents have benefited from portions of this statewide initiative. The conversions typically target residential neighborhoods, with the underground infrastructure reducing outage frequency and restoration times during major storms.

FPL has not announced a specific timeline for completing additional conversions, but the company says the 2,000-mile achievement reflects its commitment to modernizing the state's electrical grid.

item.title: Patronis votes to block AI data center costs from shifting to Florida households
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Florida's District 1 representative Jimmy Patronis has backed legislation aimed at preventing American households from footing the bill for expanding artificial intelligence data centers across the country. According to a news release, Patronis voted to advance the measure, which would shield residents from bearing infrastructure costs typically…
item.content:encoded: Florida's District 1 representative Jimmy Patronis has backed legislation aimed at preventing American households from footing the bill for expanding artificial intelligence data centers across the country. According to a news release, Patronis voted to advance the measure, which would shield residents from bearing infrastructure costs typically associated with large-scale AI facilities. The bill represents an effort by lawmakers to address concerns that deployment expenses for data centers—critical infrastructure supporting AI development—could eventually be passed along to consumers through utility costs or other means. Patronis, whose district includes Escambia County, characterized the vote as a step toward protecting local residents from unexpected financial burdens as the AI industry expands. The legislation still requires additional congressional action before becoming law.

Farris is reportedly looking to replace Gaull with Matt McKenzie, a former Baldwin County…
item.content:encoded:
Summerdale Mayor Randy Farris has placed Police Chief Michael Gaull on administrative leave and requested his resignation, according to WKRG News 5. The move has caught the city council off guard, with members saying they were blindsided by Farris's decision.

Farris is reportedly looking to replace Gaull with Matt McKenzie, a former Baldwin County Commissioner. The timing and circumstances of the administrative leave have raised questions among council members about the process being followed.

Gaull's placement on leave comes without a clear public explanation from the mayor's office about the reasons behind the decision. The situation highlights tension between the mayor and council over how the police department's leadership should be handled.

item.content:encoded: The City of Foley is moving forward with a significant infrastructure project that will add nearly two miles of new sidewalk to improve pedestrian access in the Mills community. According to a city news release obtained by WKRG News 5, the 8,700-foot sidewalk project is designed to connect the Mills area to other parts of Foley, addressing what city leaders say is a critical gap in the local pedestrian network. The project represents one of the larger infrastructure investments in the area in recent years, with officials hoping the improved walkability will benefit residents and potentially spur economic activity in the surrounding neighborhoods.

item.title: UWF Professor Earns National Award for Work With Disadvantaged Chemistry Students
item.dc:creator: newsroom

Dr. Karen Molek received the American Chemical Society's Dreyfus Award for her work encouraging underrepresented and low-income students to pursue careers in chemistry…
item.content:encoded:
A University of West Florida chemistry professor has been recognized nationally for her efforts to help economically disadvantaged students break into the chemical sciences field.

Dr. Karen Molek received the American Chemical Society's Dreyfus Award for her work encouraging underrepresented and low-income students to pursue careers in chemistry and chemical engineering. The award recognizes educators who have made a significant impact on student success and diversity in the field.

According to WKRG News 5, Molek's award reflects her commitment to expanding opportunities in STEM fields for students who might otherwise face barriers to entry. The recognition adds to UWF's growing reputation for chemical science education and workforce development in Northwest Florida.

The University of Florida says the harmless flies typically swarm in April and May, then again in August and September. Numbers can vary widely from one part of the state to another. That…
item.content:encoded: Pensacola, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- Lovebug season is underway in Florida, and drivers across the state are getting reminders every time they hit the highway. The University of Florida says the harmless flies typically swarm in April and May, then again in August and September. Numbers can vary widely from one part of the state to another. That includes Northwest Florida. The university says lovebugs were first recorded in Florida in Escambia County in 1949. They don't bite or sting, but their remains can damage car paint if they're left on too long. The advice is simple: wash them off quickly. A damp cloth or dryer sheet can help remove the mess.

Lucas reports directly to Sheriff Chip Simmons, helping shape the agency's strategic direction and policy work. She's also president of the Escambia County Sheriff Foundation, which she co-founded in 2021, and previously earned the Sheriff's Medal in 2023.

item.title: Study Links Birth Order to Disease Risk, but Experts Flag Data Gaps
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: A new study examining the connection between birth order and disease risk is raising questions about its completeness, as researchers acknowledge significant limitations in who was included in the data. The research found associations between birth order and certain health conditions, but excluded uninsured families and those on Medicaid from the…
item.content:encoded:
A new study examining the connection between birth order and disease risk is raising questions about its completeness, as researchers acknowledge significant limitations in who was included in the data.

The research found associations between birth order and certain health conditions, but excluded uninsured families and those on Medicaid from the analysis. That means a substantial portion of the U.S. population—lower-income households that may face different health challenges and barriers to care—was left out entirely.

"The findings may not tell the whole story," experts caution. Researchers say a more accurate picture of how birth order affects disease risk would require future studies to include all income levels, not just insured populations. Without that broader data, scientists risk drawing conclusions that don't apply to everyone.

The limitation underscores a recurring challenge in medical research: studies based on incomplete or skewed populations can lead to incomplete or skewed results. Health experts emphasize that understanding disease risk across birth order requires looking at the full range of American families.

item.content:encoded:
The Washington Commanders have acquired wide receiver Stefon Diggs as they look to strengthen their offensive weapons heading into the upcoming season. The move addresses a priority for the team as they work to build a more competitive receiving group.

Diggs joins a Commanders offense looking to make strides after recent seasons. His addition comes as the team continues to evaluate its roster and make moves to improve performance on the field.

The move also reflects broader conversations around receiver evaluations across the NFL. Other players in the league, including some facing questions about their fit with new teams, have drawn scrutiny from multiple franchises regarding locker room dynamics and how they might integrate with existing rosters.

The Commanders will look to integrate Diggs into their system as they prepare for the season ahead.
